unresolved_items.sentence: If new hardware, software, or infrastructure components are required to develop, test, or implement the program, these products will be coordinated through the DHS and CBP formal Technology Insertion (TI) process (to include a trade study with no less than four alternatives, one of which reflecting the status quo and another reflecting multi- agency collaboration).

rows.verbatim:
Offerors may propose an “equal” product, provided it meets or exceeds all of the salient
physical, functional, and performance characteristics specified below and elsewhere in this
SOW.
rows.normalized: Offeror may propose an 'equal' product only if it meets or exceeds all salient characteristics specified in the SOW.

rows.verbatim:
Offerors proposing an “equal” product must:
• Clearly identify the manufacturer, model, and specifications of the proposed system.
• Provide documentation and evidence demonstrating that the proposed system meets or
exceeds all salient characteristics and is fully compatible with the COTHEN HF Cellular
Network.
rows.normalized: Offeror proposing an 'equal' product must identify manufacturer/model/specs and provide documentation demonstrating equivalence and compatibility.

rows.verbatim:
If the offeror fails to provide sufficient information to demonstrate equivalence, the
Government will determine that the offeror’s product does not meet the requirements.
rows.normalized: If offeror fails to provide sufficient equivalence information, its product will be found non-compliant.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall adhere to the following applicable Federal standard /DHS/CBP/Office of
Information and Technology (OIT) policies, standards, directives, processes, and procedures in
performing work under this contract. These include, and are not limited to the following:
• The Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR): http://www.acqnet.gov/FAR/
• Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act: http://www.section508.gov/
• Homeland Security Acquisition Regulation (HSAR):
http://www.dhs.gov/xlibrary/assets/opnbiz/hsar.pdf
• Code of Federal Regulations (CFR): http://www.gpoaccess.gov/cfr/index.html
• Customs Directive No. 51715-006, Separation Procedures for Contractor Employees (CF-
242)
• CIS HB 1400-05C, “CBP Information Systems Security Policies and Procedures Handbook”
• Management Directive (MD) 4300.1, “Information Technology Systems Security Program”
• “DHS Sensitive System Policy,” Directive 4300A:
http://www.uscg.mil/hq/cg9/NAIS/RFP/SectionJ/dhs-4300A-policy.pdf
• NIST SP 800-47, “Security Guide for Interconnecting Information Technology Systems”:
http://csrc.nist.gov/publications/nistpubs/800-47/sp800-47.pdf
• DHS 4300A, “Sensitive Systems Directive”:
http://www.uscg.mil/acquisition/nais/RFP/SectionJ/dhs-4300A-handbook.pdf
rows.normalized: Contractor must adhere to listed Federal/DHS/CBP standards, policies, directives and procedures; 9 items listed.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall complete the following tasks as required to comply with this SOW.
rows.normalized: Contractor must complete the tasks described in SOW Section 4.

rows.verbatim:
The replacement radio systems must, at a minimum, provide:
• Frequency range: 1.5 to 29.9999 MHz transmit-and-receive
• Output power: 1 kW (+/-1dB) PEP and average
• Duty cycle: 100%
• Modes: SSB, ISB, CW, AM, AME Tx, WBHF
• Data rates: Waveforms supporting from 75 bps up to 240 kbps in up to 16 x 3 kHz
channels (48 kHz max. BW)
• Built-in 4G ALE
• Remote control via web browser or external remote-control software
rows.normalized: Replacement radio systems must provide at minimum the listed frequency, power, duty cycle, modes, data rate, ALE, and remote control capabilities (continues on next page).

rows.verbatim:
• Compliance with MIL-STD-188-110D and MIL-STD-188-141D
• Interoperability with the existing COTHEN High Frequency Cellular Network, including
compatibility with Collins Aerospace software and protocols currently in use
• All other specifications and requirements listed in this SOW
rows.normalized: Continuation of salient characteristics list: MIL-STD compliance, COTHEN interoperability, and all other SOW specifications.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall test and functionally certify all equipment prior to delivery to ensure
compliance and specifications.
rows.normalized: Contractor must test and functionally certify all equipment before delivery.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall deliver equipment as outlined below.
rows.normalized: Contractor must deliver equipment per the schedule outlined in Section 5.

rows.verbatim: The equipment shall be shipped to the address provided in section 5.1.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ship equipment to the address in Section 5.1.

rows.verbatim: Receiver-Transmitter Radio System:
rows.normalized: Receiver-Transmitter Radio System specification table, pages 5-6, listing approximately 24 technical characteristics (data rate, RF output, control, power, temperature, humidity).

rows.verbatim:
The Government Purchase Order number must be reflected on the Shipping label and clearly
delineated on the packing slip(s).
rows.normalized: Contractor must put the Government Purchase Order number on shipping label and packing slips.

rows.verbatim: MFG P/N Manufacturer Description QTY
rows.normalized: Bill of Materials line-item table, page 7, listing 5 items (radio system, cables/connectors, software, shipping, warranty) with quantities.

rows.verbatim:
Absence of any comments by the COR does not relieve the Contractor
of the responsibility for complying with the requirements of the Task Order.
rows.normalized: Contractor remains responsible for complying with Task Order requirements regardless of COR comments.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall have five (5) business days to make corrections and redeliver.
rows.normalized: Contractor must make corrections and redeliver within 5 business days of non-acceptance.

rows.verbatim: Should the Government fail to complete the review within the review period the deliverable will be considered “Accepted”.
rows.normalized: If Government misses its review period, the deliverable is automatically deemed accepted (deadline dependency affecting contractor).

rows.verbatim: Any such proposed changes must be brought to the immediate attention of the CO for action.
rows.normalized: Contractor must bring any proposed changes to the CO's immediate attention.

rows.verbatim:
The acceptance of any changes by the contractor without specific approval and written consent of the CO
shall be at the contractor’s risk.
rows.normalized: Contractor bears the risk if it accepts changes without the CO's written approval.

rows.verbatim:
Payment requests shall be submitted electronically through the U. S. Department of the
Treasury's Invoice Processing Platform System (IPP).
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit payment requests electronically via IPP.

rows.verbatim:
If the Contractor is unable to comply with the requirement to use IPP for submitting
invoices for payment, the Contractor must submit a waiver request in writing to the
Contracting Officer.
rows.normalized: If Contractor cannot use IPP, it must submit a written waiver request to the CO.

rows.verbatim:
Please ensure the following are included in all invoices:
• Purchase Order number
• Description of services provided for a specified time period.
• Unit price and total amount of each item.
• Discount terms
• Company name, telephone number, taxpayer’s identification number, and
complete mailing address to which payment will be mailed.
rows.normalized: Contractor must include listed items (PO number, service description, pricing, discount terms, company info) in all invoices.

rows.verbatim:
A courtesy e-mail notification upon invoice submission in IPP shall be sent by the
Contractor to the COR.
rows.normalized: Contractor must send a courtesy email notification to the COR upon IPP invoice submission.

rows.verbatim: All contract questions and concerns shall be directed to the point of contracts as designated below.
rows.normalized: Contract questions/concerns must be directed to the designated point of contact.

rows.verbatim:
The Offeror shall ensure that the design conforms to the Department of Homeland Security
(DHS) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) Enterprise Architecture (EA), the DHS and
CBP Technical Reference Models (TRM), and all DHS and CBP policies and guidelines (such as
the CBP Information Technology Enterprise Principles and the DHS Service Oriented
Architecture - Technical Framework), as promulgated by the DHS and CBP Chief Information
Officers (CIO), Chief Technology Officers (CTO) and Chief Architects (CA).
rows.normalized: Offeror must ensure design conforms to DHS/CBP EA, TRM, and policies/guidelines.

rows.verbatim:
The Offeror shall conform to the Federal Enterprise Architecture (FEA) model and the DHS and
CBP versions of the FEA model, as described in their respective EAs.
rows.normalized: Offeror must conform to FEA model and DHS/CBP versions of it.

rows.verbatim:
All models will be submitted using Business Process Modeling Notation (BPMN 1.1 or BPMN
2.0 when available) and the CBP Architectural Modeling Standards.
rows.normalized: Offeror's models must be submitted using BPMN and CBP Architectural Modeling Standards.

rows.verbatim:
Data semantics shall be in conformance with the National Information Exchange Model
(NIEM).
rows.normalized: Data semantics must conform to NIEM.

rows.verbatim:
Development solutions will also ensure compliance with the current version of the DHS and
CBP target architectures.
rows.normalized: Development solutions must comply with current DHS/CBP target architectures.

rows.verbatim:
Where possible, the Offeror shall use DHS/CBP approved products, standards, services, and
profiles, as reflected by the hardware, software, application, and infrastructure components of the
DHS/CBP TRM/standards profile.
rows.normalized: Offeror must use DHS/CBP approved products/standards/services/profiles where possible.

rows.verbatim: All developed solutions shall be compliant with the Homeland Security (HLS) EA.
rows.normalized: All developed solutions must comply with the HLS EA.

rows.verbatim: All IT hardware and software shall be compliant with the HLS EA.
rows.normalized: All IT hardware/software must comply with the HLS EA.

rows.verbatim: Compliance with the HLS EA shall be derived from and aligned through the CBP EA.
rows.normalized: HLS EA compliance must be derived from and aligned through the CBP EA.

rows.verbatim:
Description information for all data assets, information exchanges and data standards, whether
adopted or developed, shall be submitted to the Enterprise Data Management Office (EDMO) for
review, approval, and insertion into the DHS Data Reference Model and Enterprise Architecture
Information Repository.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit data asset/exchange/standard description information to EDMO for review and insertion into DHS repositories.

rows.verbatim:
Development of data assets, information exchanges, and data standards will comply with the
DHS Data Management Policy MD 103-01.
rows.normalized: Development of data assets/exchanges/standards must comply with DHS MD 103-01.

rows.verbatim:
All data-related artifacts will be developed and validated according to DHS Data Management
Architectural Guidelines.
rows.normalized: All data-related artifacts must be developed and validated per DHS Data Management Architectural Guidelines.

rows.verbatim:
Applicability of Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6) to DHS-related components (networks,
infrastructure, and applications) specific to individual acquisitions shall be in accordance with
the DHS EA (per OMB Memorandum M-05-22, August 2, 2005), regardless of whether the
acquisition is for modification, upgrade, or replacement.
rows.normalized: IPv6 applicability to DHS components must be in accordance with the DHS EA regardless of acquisition type.

rows.verbatim:
All EA related component acquisitions shall be IPv6 compliant, as defined in the USGv6 Profile
(NIST Special Publication 500-267) and the corresponding declarations of conformance, defined
in the USGv6 Test Program.
rows.normalized: All EA-related component acquisitions must be IPv6 compliant per USGv6 Profile and Test Program.

rows.verbatim:
All products, platforms and services delivered as part of this work statement that, by definition,
are deemed ICT shall conform to the revised regulatory implementation of Section 508
Standards, which are located at 36 C.F.R. § 1194.1 & Appendixes A, C & D, and available
at https://www.ecfr.gov/cgi-bin/text-
idx?SID=e1c6735e25593339a9db63534259d8ec&mc=true&node=pt36.3.1194&rgn=div5.
rows.normalized: All ICT products/platforms/services delivered under this work statement must conform to Section 508 Standards (36 CFR 1194.1 & Appendixes A,C,D).

rows.verbatim: Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act (classified to 29 U.S.C. § 794d) requires that when Federal agencies develop, procure, maintain, or use information and communications technology (ICT), it shall be accessible to people with disabilities.

rows.verbatim: Federal employees and members of the public with disabilities must be afforded access to and use of information and data comparable to that of Federal employees and members of the public without disabilities.
rows.normalized: Found by the coverage check and not by the reader: Federal employees and members of the public with disabilities must be afforded access to and use of information and data comparable to that of Federal employees and members of the public without disabilities.

rows.verbatim:
Any request for additional exceptions shall be sent to the
Contracting Officer and a determination will be made according to DHS Directive 139-05,
Office of Accessible Systems and Technology, dated November 12, 2018 and DHS Instruction
139-05-001, Managing the Accessible Systems and Technology Program, dated November 20,
2018, or any successor publication.
rows.normalized: Any request for additional Section 508 exceptions must be sent to the Contracting Officer.

rows.verbatim:
All hardware, software, and services provided under this task order must be compliant with DHS
4300A DHS Sensitive System Policy and the DHS 4300A Sensitive Directive Handbook.
rows.normalized: All hardware/software/services provided under the task order must comply with DHS 4300A policy and handbook.

rows.verbatim:
If encryption is require, the following methods are acceptable for encrypting sensitive
information:
1. FIPS 197 (Advanced Encryption Standard (AES)) 256 algorithm and cryptographic
modules that have been validated under FIPS 140-2.
2. National Security Agency (NSA) Type 2 or Type 1 encryption.
3. Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) (see paragraph 5.5.2.1 of the Department of
Homeland Security (DHS) IT Security Program Handbook (DHS Management
Directive (MD) 4300A) for Sensitive Systems).
rows.normalized: If encryption is required, contractor must use one of the three listed acceptable encryption methods (FIPS 197/AES, NSA Type 1/2, or PKI).

rows.verbatim: Any request for additional exceptions shall be sent to the Contracting Officer and a determination will be made according to DHS Directive 139-05, Office of Accessible Systems and Technology, dated November 12, 2018 and DHS Instruction 139-05-001, Managing the Accessible Systems and Technology Program, dated November 20, 2018, or any successor document.
